briefFidelity: FAIL, and it is not close. The brief asks for BARROW: a monumental, brutalist, immovable single mass, heavier than the frame comfortably holds, charcoal and iron with a SINGLE OCHRE SEAM, built from a few large members. Before I read a word of it I described these sheets as 'a centred radial rosette', 'a rose window', 'a sunflower head', 'a coin seen through falling ash'. The words heavy, monument, mound, immovable and brutalist did not occur to me once across five sheets. Four requirements fail independently. (1) FORM: every seed is n-fold radially symmetric - 1310661 and 1283437 are six-fold, 1203347 and 1475115 seven-fold - and radial symmetry is precisely what makes an object read as ornament rather than as mass. A barrow is not a mandala. (2) PALETTE INVERSION: ochre is not a seam here, it is the entire subject in eleven of twelve seeds; the charcoal and iron have been demoted to background confetti in the corners. There is no seam anywhere in the collection - no linear accent of any kind exists in the vocabulary. 1985692 is the only seed where iron dominates the mass and it is an outlier, not the rule. (3) CONSTRUCTION: the brief says a few large members, not many small ones, and 1243682, 1283437, 1561509 and 1985692 are built from hundreds of small squares with a fizzing granular fringe. (4) SCALE: 1446330 is a speck in a near-empty black frame and 1561509 is barely larger; neither commands the frame, let alone exceeds it. The work is accomplished. It is not this brief.
composition: There is a clear focal hierarchy and it is the same hierarchy twelve times: an amber core dead centre, a grey debris field thinning inward from the corners, a black moat between them (cleanest in 1310661 and 1835793). The core dominates and that dominance is plainly deliberate. But the frame is never used - every token is a bullseye, the subject floats at the exact centre in all twelve, and nothing is ever cropped, weighted low, or pushed against an edge on purpose. Against a brief demanding a form larger than the frame holds, only 1203347, 1475115 and 1991107 press the edges at all, and even they stop politely short. 1446330 and 1561509 float in empty black with no relationship to the frame whatsoever.
collectionCoherence: Strong, and the strongest axis here. All twelve share one ground, one mark (the rotated translucent square, and nothing else), one two-family palette, one centred radial construction, and one debris behaviour. Laid out on the contact sheet 1203347, 1446330, 1985692 and 1991107 are obviously siblings despite being the four most different tokens in the set. If anything the coherence is oversupplied: the invariant centring means the sheet reads as one stamp at twelve settings rather than as twelve works, and there is no compositional idea anywhere that distinguishes one token from another.
palette: On its own terms the colour is chosen and handsome: a dull brass ochre against a slate blue-grey, both on a near-black that is very slightly cool, with the grey squares held at low contrast so the debris field reads as weather rather than as competing subject. The ground supports the drawing everywhere except 1985692, where the grey population lies over the amber and the token turns muddy. But the brief's palette instruction is a hierarchy, not a list, and the hierarchy is inverted: charcoal and iron were to be the body and ochre a single seam. Here ochre is the body in 1203347, 1310661, 1475115, 1835793 and 1991107, and iron never forms a mass at all. Having the right three colours in the wrong roles is not the palette that was asked for.
seedVariation: Genuinely good, and the axis this work would win on under a different brief. The twelve vary on three real axes rather than by rotation: core scale (1203347, 1475115 and 1991107 fill the frame; 1446330 and 1561509 are tiny), granularity (the flat opaque slabs of 1203347 and 1835793 against the hundreds of small squares in 1243682, 1283437 and 1561509), and cool-family invasion (1985692 fully overtaken, 1366079 half-overtaken with dark squares set into the amber like inclusions). These are different works, not one work twelve times. The one convergence is at the top of the size range, where 1203347, 1475115 and 1991107 differ only in point count and rotation.
thumbnailSurvival: Reads adequately at 120px, because what carries is silhouette and mass rather than interior detail. 1446330 (near-empty), 1561509 (tiny speckled), 1985692 (grey, not gold) and 1366079 (perforated) are each identifiable at a glance, and the fuzzy rim of 1243682 and 1283437 still separates from the hard edge of 1310661. Two failures: the large solid seeds 1203347, 1475115 and 1991107 collapse into one another as 'amber polygon on black', and the interior inclusions of 1366079 turn to mush. Measured against the brief's own test - that a few large members should make it read as ONE SILHOUETTE at browse size - only the solid seeds pass; 1243682, 1283437 and 1561509 read as a cloud of grain with no silhouette at all.
marketResponse: Highly visible, and I recorded the state arc blind before reading anything - but the change delivered is not the change the brief claims. The brief says the mass FRACTURES under drawdown, members separating, silhouette breaking. On 1283437 stress and 1310661 stress the object does the opposite: it doubles in size, brightens, and resolves into a dense concentric mandala with a black hexagonal aperture opening at the centre - more ordered, more ornate and more complete than its own neutral, which is a bloom, not a break. Only 1203347 stress and 1243682 stress support the fracture reading, and even there the core grows rather than redistributing, so mass appears to be created rather than separated. Recovery does not consolidate either: 1283437 recovery and 1310661 recovery are more speckled and more scattered at the rim than their own neutral frames. The claimed behaviour is inverted on half the seeds shown.
tokenIdentity: Broadly holds, with one strain. Symmetry order, palette and centring persist across all three states, so 1310661 stays a six-fold hexagonal object in neutral, stress and recovery, and 1283437 stays six-fold and granular throughout - these are recognisably one token under three conditions. The strain is 1203347, where neutral is a compact clean seven-point slab and stress is a frame-filling explosion of roughly double the mass; at 120px those two frames are close to reading as two different objects rather than one object in two moods. 1243682 has the same problem to a lesser degree. Identity survives, but by symmetry order and hue rather than by silhouette.
artifacts: Frame clipping in the stress row: amber squares are cut hard by the left and top edges in 1203347 stress and by the left and right edges in 1243682 stress. It may be intended as overflow but it reads as the viewBox cutting the work rather than the work exceeding the frame. 1446330 is so sparse it reads as under-drawn rather than as restraint - a near-empty tile that would look like a rendering failure beside its neighbours. 1985692 is the one legibility casualty: the grey squares stacked over the amber turn the core to mush at 120px. In 1366079 the dark squares set inside the amber body read ambiguously, as dirt as readily as inclusions. Nothing here is broken, but the clipping and 1446330's emptiness are both visible defects on the sheet.
reasoning: This is competent, coherent, well-varied work and it is not the work that was commissioned. I wrote my description before opening the brief and it contains the words rosette, rose window, sunflower, coin, medallion and mandala, and does not contain the words heavy, monument, mound, immovable or brutalist anywhere. That gap is the finding. The single structural decision that causes it is the n-fold radial symmetry present in every seed: radial symmetry produces ornament, and BARROW asked for mass. On top of that the specified palette hierarchy is exactly inverted - ochre was to be a single seam over charcoal and iron, and instead ochre is the entire subject in eleven of twelve seeds while iron is background confetti - the 'few large members' rule is broken outright by the granular construction of 1243682, 1283437 and 1561509, the 'larger than the frame comfortably holds' requirement is contradicted by 1446330 and 1561509 floating in empty black, and the claimed fracture-under-drawdown inverts into a bloom on 1283437 and 1310661. briefFidelity is a gate and it fails on four independent counts, so the verdict is REFUSE regardless of how good the seed variation is. I am not refusing this for failing to be some other artwork I would have preferred; I am refusing it for being a rose window where a burial mound was specified.
wouldChange: Break the radial symmetry first - it is the single decision doing the damage, and nothing else can be fixed while it stands. Replace the n-fold rosette with an asymmetric stacked mass: a small number of large quadrilateral members resting on and shouldering into each other, weighted toward the lower frame, cropped by the bottom and side edges so the form is read as continuing beyond the viewBox. Swap the colour roles: make the charcoal and iron squares the body of the object at large scale, and reduce the ochre to one narrow continuous run threading between members - a seam, one per token, not a fill. Kill the small-square fringe entirely; the grain in 1243682, 1283437 and 1561509 is what prevents a silhouette from forming at 120px. Raise the floor on core scale so 1446330 and 1561509 cannot render as specks in an empty frame. Then rebuild the state response so drawdown separates the existing members along their contact seams - same members, same total mass, gaps opening between them, the ochre seam widening as they part - and recovery closes those gaps, instead of the current behaviour where stress adds mass and brightness and 1283437 and 1310661 become denser and more ornate under stress than they are at rest.
